asks.notes: Section B: the "PREPARATORY WORK" (scale and chord bank) is MARKED at Ordinary Level ("Grid", 1 mark per correct note of chord, 12), so its heading and bullets are part of the question text (coordinator ruling: "PREPARATORY WORK • ...") and its line is a counted criterion. The chord bank prints I ("The first chord is given") and also iii and vii° already filled in and shaded, outside the five chords asked for: the 12 notes are those of ii, IV, V and vi; the pre-filled chords are part of the printed question, not separate asks. The "1 x 12" / "3 x 4" / "2 x 12" sit in the scheme’s Mark column, so the labels carry the descriptor only; each "1 mark per ... (1 x 12)" line is counted and each "Up to 3 marks for quality ... (3 x 4)" line a no-band criterion on 0-12. JUDGEMENT CALL (not in the format): the 2017 Ordinary scheme marks its "2 x 12" elements on ALTERNATIVE per-item rates joined by a printed "OR" (2 marks a good note / chord, OR 1 mark when the rhythm is not used / the chord only fits). A counted line at rate 2 (0, 2, 4 ... 24) could not place the odd totals the 1-mark alternative gives, so each such element is a no-band criterion on 0-24, labelled with the scheme’s element name ("Bass" / "Chords") and carrying its printed lines, "OR" included, as guidance. The 2017 Ordinary scheme prints NO Section B general points and NO table of given or accepted chords, so there are no task requirements and no scheme crop. The title is printed in capitals and kept so, without the "Q." number. Grid 12 + Melody 12 + 12 + Bass 24 = 60. Q4’s (i)-(iv) name the cadences at A-D (the cadence words print in bold); one ask, one total. The booklet’s title has no "AT CADENCE POINTS" (the scheme’s heading adds it); the paper’s words are used. Key D major, 3/4; the given rhythm (minim, crotchet, dotted minim) is printed over each cadence.
